terms.gloss: the third syllable from the end
evidence: Diom. p. 425 P.; Mart. Cap. 3 (Lewis & Short s.v. antepaenultimus)
terms.comment: The stress falls on the antepenult when the penult is short: In quā syllabā accentum pōnimus sī paenultima syllaba est brevis? — In antepaenultimā syllabā. (Traupman 238).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 237, p. 238, p. 245.
